U1-S1: measurement relationships as meaning-bearing models; no required computation formula
U1-S2: qualitative Newton I; $\Sigma F=0$ when forces balance; weight/support comparisons when source-supported
U1-S3: one-dimensional vector sum / $F_{net}$; scaled arrow magnitude and direction
U1-S4: equilibrium rule $\Sigma F=0$ in horizontal/vertical directions
U1-S5: select among net-force/equilibrium/vector relationships only after modeling the system
U2-S1: motion is relative to a stated reference frame; no formula by default
U2-S2: $v=d/t$ and average velocity/displacement relationships when source-supported
U2-S3: $a=\Delta v/\Delta t$; interpret sign/direction before arithmetic
U2-S4: $v=gt$ and $d=\tfrac12 gt^2$ for free fall from rest under the course approximation; distinguish how fast vs how far
U2-S5: velocity-vector addition/components appropriate to the course level
U3-S1: $F_{net}=ma$; proportional reasoning among force, mass, acceleration
U3-S2: $F_{net}=F_{applied}-F_{friction}$ in simple 1-D models; friction evidence before calculation
U3-S4: Newton III force pairs: equal magnitude/opposite direction on different objects
U3-S5: horizontal constant velocity + vertical free-fall relationships; component reasoning
U4-S2: $\sum p_{before}=\sum p_{after}$ for an appropriately defined system with negligible external impulse
U4-S4: $PE_g=mgh$ and mechanical-energy conservation when assumptions fit
U4-S5: efficiency/input-output energy relationships and evidence-based comparisons
U5-S2: superposition/interference/standing-wave relationships; emphasize diagrams before formula
U5-S4: echo distance $d=vt/2$ when applicable; resonance/natural-frequency relations
U6-S3: $n=c/v$; Snell/critical-angle relationships only to the level required by the Assessment Plan/source
U6-S4: thin-lens/image relationships and magnification only when source-supported; ray diagrams remain primary
U6-S5: select optical principles/relationships for real devices rather than equation hunting
U7-S1: charge conservation/interaction; Coulomb-type quantitative relationships only when explicitly supported by plan/source
U7-S2: voltage as energy per charge; current as charge flow, e.g. $I=Q/t$ when used
U7-S4: $P=IV$ and $E=Pt$; connect ratings to energy use/cost where useful
U7-S5: series/parallel equivalent resistance and current/voltage reasoning at course level
U8-S1: field/pole/domain models; no formula by default
U8-S2: magnetic field around current-carrying wire/loop/coil; direction models
U8-S3: magnetic force on moving charge/current-carrying wire only at source-supported quantitative level; prioritize direction/system model
U8-S4: Faraday/generator relationships conceptually; AC cycle/graph interpretation
U8-S5: transformer/system input-output relationships when source-supported; energy transformations across components
